natural_body: Price-sensitive SMB 40% off: signups +31%, rev +18%, retention -12%.

first.rationale: Two of three current problems (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) map directly onto durable, previously-validated internal levers (memory_31, memory_86, memory_91) with no recorded retention harm, whereas the competitor pricing pressure tempts a promotional_pricing response that memory_73 shows drove signups/revenue up but retention down 12% — a direct threat to the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. I verify memory_73 to confirm that tradeoff still holds before ruling pricing out, and memory_86 to confirm the onboarding-shortening result before committing this week's single experiment slot to it. Given only one experiment is possible, I favor addressing the metric with clearest causal lever and no known downstream harm (onboarding) rather than chasing the competitor on price, which risks repeating a known retention cost. I'm not treating this as fully settled — competitor dynamics could change the calculus next cycle — so I keep scale at a standard (not broad) experiment to preserve optionality and re-evaluate pricing response separately.
